claims.text: Take a straight bar on a low pulley, hands about shoulder width or slightly wider, palms facing down.

quotes.text: Grab a cable bar attachment that is fastened to a low pulley. Your hands should be shoulder width apart, or slightly wider if you wish. Your hands should be facing down.

claims.text: Stand close to the pulley with the arms extended in front holding the bar; that is the start.

quotes.text: Stand close to the pulley and extend your arms in front of you while holding the bar. This is the starting position.

claims.text: Elevate the shoulders to lift the bar as high as possible, breathing out, and hold the top for a second.

quotes.text: Elevating your shoulders, lift the bar as high as you possibly can. Exhale while performing this motion. Hold the contraction at the top for a second.

claims.text: Stand up straight, head up, eyes forward.

quotes.text: Stand up straight while performing the exercise.
Keep your head up and eyes facing forward throughout.

claims.text: Do not lift the bar with the biceps; only the shoulders move up and down.

quotes.text: Do not use your biceps to lift the bar. Your shoulders should be the only part of your body moving up and down during the exercise.

claims.text: Lower the bar back to the start.

quotes.text: Lower the bar to its original position.

claims.text: Tempo: about 1-2 s up and 1-2 s down, with a one-second hold at the top and a slow lowering.

quotes.text: using 3- to 5-min rest periods between sets performed at a moderate contraction velocity (1-2 s CON; 1-2 s ECC).
Hold the contraction at the top for a second.
lowering slowly to the original starting position.

claims.text: The shrug is an isolation exercise for the muscles that lift the shoulder girdle, such as the upper trapezius (barbell source; same movement on a cable).

quotes.text: The shrug is an isolation exercise for the muscles that lifts and supports your shoulder girdle, like the top portion of your trapezius among others.

claims.text: Only raise and lower the shoulders; do not roll them.

quotes.text: focus on only raising/lowering the shoulders - DO NOT roll the shoulders.

claims.text: Wrap the thumbs around the handle or bar.

quotes.text: Perform all grips with your thumbs around the bar.

claims.text: Grip strength drops when the wrist bends away from its natural slightly-extended position (measured on grip, applied here as a wrist cue).

quotes.text: Grip strength is significantly reduced when wrist position deviates from this self-selected optimum position.

claims.text: Add load in small steps (2-10%) only once the target reps are exceeded by one or two.

quotes.text: When training at a specific RM load, it is recommended that 2-10% increase in load be applied when the individual can perform the current workload for one to two repetitions over the desired number.

claims.text: Heavy lifting with a held breath (Valsalva) drives blood pressure very high.

quotes.text: It was concluded that when healthy young subjects perform weight-lifting exercises the mechanical compression of blood vessels combines with a potent pressor response and a Valsalva response to produce extreme elevations in blood pressure.

claims.text: The shoulder is one of the most common injury sites in resistance training (up to 36% of documented injuries), and poor technique is a named risk factor.

quotes.text: The results of the review indicated that up to 36% of documented RT-related injuries and disorders occur at the shoulder complex.
extrinsic risk factors, namely, that of improper attention to exercise technique.

claims.text: In EMG studies the shrug gives very high upper-trapezius activity: the one-arm shrug was the highest of ten exercises in healthy adults, and the shrug the highest of five in women with neck muscle pain (implement not stated in either abstract).

quotes.text: The unilateral shoulder shrug exercise was found to produce the greatest EMG activity in the upper trapezius.
For the trapezius muscle, the highest level of muscle activation was found during the shrug (102+/-11% of MVC), lateral raise (97+/-6% of MVC), and upright row (85+/-5% of MVC) exercises

plate.viewWhy: Straight arms, the upright body and the straight-up shoulder path read side-on (c2, c4, c5); the census draws it side, like the parent.
plate.equipment: Cable column with the pulley at the bottom; straight bar held in front of the thighs, lifter standing close to the column so the cable runs nearly straight down (c1, c2); floor line.
plate.start: Standing up straight, head up (c4), arms extended holding the bar in front (c2), shoulders relaxed down.
plate.end: Same body; shoulders lifted as high as they go (c3), arms still straight (c5).
